plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $31, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $31, ensuring I maximize expected profit without risk of overpaying.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - you never pay more than your value if you win, and bidding truthfully maximizes your expected profit. Since my value is $37, I should bid exactly $37. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay only that second-highest amount, guaranteeing non-negative profit whenever I win.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid), so bidding higher than your value risks overpaying, while bidding lower reduces your chance of winning profitable auctions. With my value at $11, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $11, ensuring I only win when it's profitable and maximize expected value.
